text:
alex: FYI: multiple hosted-api customers reporting elevated 5xx/timeout errors on /v1/generate in region-east starting ~14:07 UTC. Large fraction are 504s. Investigating.

jess: Yep, we started seeing 504s at 14:08 from our prod service. simple POST to /v1/generate -> 504. No schema changes on our side. Sample curl:

jess: ```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \ 
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" \ 
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \ 
  -d '{"model":"rwd-13b","prompt":"Explain event-driven architectures"}'
```

natalie: I pulled proxy traces for hosted-east. Proxy shows 10s upstream timeouts to runtime processes, correlating with spikes in redis/prefix-cache latency (200-800ms). A few requests show `ioredis: read ECONNRESET` and some `LOADING`/`MOVED` responses.

maria: Infra monitoring: redis cluster experienced IO wait and eviction bursts at 14:05-14:20. There were also TCP retransmits on node-2. Sentinel reported a temporary failover attempt that didn't complete cleanly.

tim: From runtime logs: the generation pipeline does a prefix-KV lookup synchronously before model scheduling. When the cache client blocks, batch formation stalls and the runtime hits the API gateway deadline and returns 502/504. I'm also seeing `BlockingRedisCommand` stacktraces and backlog counters rising.

alex: Impact: hosted inference customers in region-east using prefix caching affected. Severity P1. Ryan, please post a status page that we have degraded responses and we're investigating.

ryan: On it. Drafting a message now. ETA unknown, advising customers to retry and that engineering is investigating.

infra-bot: ALERT: redis-prod-cluster latency >250ms, node-2 retransmits detected, 14:06 UTC.

deploy-bot: incident-tracker: created incident CH-INC-20260315-17.

maria: Immediate mitigations to consider:
- disable prefix cache read path for generation traffic in region-east (fallback to model call only)
- enable client-side short-circuit for cache on timeout
- route eligible traffic to warm dedicated pools if customer consented to cross-region
- apply emergency failover of unhealthy redis node

tim: I can push a runtime flag that makes prefix cache lookups async with a strict deadline (150ms) and otherwise skip the cache. That should be quick and low-risk.

alex: Do that. Maria/infra, can you try failover or restart of the problematic redis node? Please call out if a restore will cause additional load.

maria: Starting controlled failover of redis node-2 to standby at 14:18 UTC. I'll also temporarily mark eviction policy to reduce churn and disable scheduled backup for 30m if it's running.

deploy-bot: featureflag-service deploy started -> rollout/disable-prefix-kv-east. 14:20 UTC.

deploy-bot: rollout complete on 6 hosts (14:21 UTC).

tim: Runtime change applied: cache lookups now async with 150ms deadline for generation flows. Observability flags emit metric `cache.fallback` when triggered.

natalie: After the flag, proxy upstream latencies drop within ~30s. Error rate for affected customers down ~85% and retries generally succeed.

jess: Confirmed on our end — error rate dropped to baseline within a minute after the change. Thanks. RID sample: rq_aa7c3e. I'll DM the id.

maria: Failover completed and node-2 removed from primary set at 14:25. We're seeing reduced IO wait. We'll run a full reshard check and investigate root cause (candidate: overlapping snapshot/backup + eviction storm on small-memory instance).

tim: Follow-ups: PR to implement non-blocking cache client with configurable deadline and circuit-breaker counters; add defensive ioredis client defaults (`maxRetriesPerRequest=1`, `connectTimeout=1500ms`); metric `cache.fallback.rate` on dashboards.

alex: Actions assigned: tim -> runtime patch + PR; maria/infra -> redis RCA + reshard/ops playbook; ryan -> customer comms and incident update; natalie -> expand synthetic checks to include cache-path latency. Jess we'll follow up with a detailed incident email.

ryan: Posting an update to the status page: mitigation applied (cache reads disabled/async) at 14:21 UTC; ongoing: redis cluster stabilization; next update + postmortem in 24h.

maria: Scheduling rolling restart of redis-prod nodes 14:40-15:10 UTC after reshard verification. Created ticket INFRA-3799 for backup schedule review.

tim: Repro steps I used locally to simulate the issue (engineering):

```
# simulate high redis latency on a runtime node
sudo tc qdisc add dev lo root netem delay 300ms 50ms distribution normal
# run load against local runtime with prefix cache enabled
wrk -t4 -c50 -d60s --latency http://localhost:8080/v1/generate -s scripts/chat.lua
```

alex: Marking incident mitigated (prefix cache async/disabled) at 14:22 UTC. We'll keep monitoring. If anyone sees residual 5xxs, ping here with request ids.

jess: Thanks for fast response. Please include steps we can use to detect similar problems on our side (we have logs but would prefer actionable traces). I'll include the sample rids.

maria: Will provide trace links and postmortem with timeline, root cause, and corrective actions. Preliminary root cause: redis eviction + partial partition under backup/compaction causing blocking cache client calls.

tim: I'll submit a small runtime change to master tomorrow and include e2e test that forces cache timeouts to ensure we always fallback fast.

infra-bot: Monitoring: redis cluster stable, no further alerts as of 14:48 UTC.

alex: Great work everyone. Closing the channel for active mitigation; we'll reopen for postmortem comments. :thumbsup:
